questions.q: Which option contains only correctly matched Meghalaya districts and their headquarters?
o: North Garo Hills—Resubelpara; East Jaintia Hills—Khliehriat; South West Khasi Hills—Mawkyrwat; West Jaintia Hills—Jowai
North Garo Hills—Baghmara; East Jaintia Hills—Jowai; South West Khasi Hills—Nongpoh; West Jaintia Hills—Khliehriat
North Garo Hills—Williamnagar; East Jaintia Hills—Mawkyrwat; South West Khasi Hills—Jowai; West Jaintia Hills—Resubelpara
North Garo Hills—Ampati; East Jaintia Hills—Nongstoin; South West Khasi Hills—Baghmara; West Jaintia Hills—Khliehriat
questions.e: The Meghalaya Government's district table lists Resubelpara for North Garo Hills, Khliehriat for East Jaintia Hills, Mawkyrwat for South West Khasi Hills and Jowai for West Jaintia Hills. The other options interchange headquarters from different districts.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against Meghalaya Government — Districts and headquarters (Statistical Handbook 2022).
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Meghalaya Government — Districts and headquarters (Statistical Handbook 2022)

questions.q: Meghalaya has 60 Legislative Assembly constituencies. How are they distributed between the Khasi-Jaintia Hills and Garo Hills divisions?
o: 36 in Khasi-Jaintia Hills and 24 in Garo Hills
24 in Khasi-Jaintia Hills and 36 in Garo Hills
40 in Khasi-Jaintia Hills and 20 in Garo Hills
questions.e: The Elections Department profile records 36 Assembly constituencies in the Khasi-Jaintia Hills division and 24 in the Garo Hills division. These figures add to the State Assembly's total of 60 seats and are a division-wise distribution.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against Meghalaya Government — Elections Department / Chief Electoral Officer.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Meghalaya Government — Elections Department / Chief Electoral Officer

questions.q: The Kynshi River forms Nongkhnum island by diverging into which two named streams?
o: Namliang to the north and Phanliang to the south
Phanliang to the north and Namliang to the south
Rilang to the north and Kynshi to the south
Umiam to the north and Myntdu to the south
questions.e: The official West Khasi Hills profile states that the Kynshi diverges near Diangsyiang and Diligim villages. Its northern branch is Namliang and its southern branch is Phanliang; the island lies between the channels.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against Meghalaya Government — West Khasi Hills / Nongstoin district profile.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Meghalaya Government — West Khasi Hills / Nongstoin district profile

questions.q: How many Community and Rural Development blocks does the Meghalaya Government's East Khasi Hills district profile list?
questions.e: The East Khasi Hills profile lists eight C&RD blocks: Mylliem, Mawphlang, Khatarshnong Laitkroh, Shellabholaganj, Mawsynram, Pynursla, Mawryngkneng and Mawkynrew. The count is specific to the district profile.

questions.q: According to the East Khasi Hills profile, which district was carved out of East Khasi Hills on 4 June 1992?
questions.e: The profile records that East Khasi Hills was further divided into East Khasi Hills and Ri-Bhoi on 4 June 1992. This date concerns district reorganisation and should not be confused with the creation of other Meghalaya districts.

questions.e: The Elections Department profile expressly places the Chief Electoral Officer's office under the superintendence, directions and control of the Election Commission of India. Its work includes electoral rolls, EPICs and election administration.

questions.q: The Meghalaya Government describes Kyllang Rock near Mawnai as a single huge solid rock of which geological origin?
questions.e: The West Khasi Hills profile describes Kyllang Rock as a single, huge solid igneous rock near Mawnai. Igneous rocks form when molten material cools and solidifies; the question tests the official description, not local folklore.

o: About seven to eight fish ponds
questions.e: The official profile notes a depression on the peak with about seven to eight fish ponds of considerable size. This is a location-specific fact about Mawthadraishan, distinct from the district's river-island and waterfall descriptions.

questions.q: Under Article 143, the President may seek the Supreme Court's opinion on a question of law or fact that is of what character?
o: Such public importance that it is expedient to obtain the Court's opinion
Only a question already decided by a trial court
Only a dispute between two private companies
Any routine administrative question without public importance
questions.e: Article 143 creates an advisory jurisdiction. The President may refer a question of law or fact of public importance, and the Supreme Court may report its opinion after such hearing as it thinks fit.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against India Code — Constitution of India.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: For Parliament to legislate on a State List matter in the national interest under Article 249, what support must a Rajya Sabha resolution receive?
o: Not less than two-thirds of members present and voting
A simple majority of the total membership of both Houses
Unanimous approval of all State Legislatures
Two-thirds of the members of the Lok Sabha only
questions.e: Article 249 requires a resolution supported by not less than two-thirds of Rajya Sabha members present and voting. While the resolution remains in force, Parliament may legislate on the specified State List matter in the national interest.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against India Code — Constitution of India.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: Which pair of Bills is not subject to the ordinary joint-sitting procedure under Article 108?
o: Money Bills and Constitution Amendment Bills
Private Members' Bills and Government Bills
Bills passed by both Houses without disagreement
questions.e: Article 108 excludes Money Bills from joint sittings. A Constitution Amendment Bill must separately secure the special majority in each House under Article 368, so disagreement cannot be resolved by an ordinary joint sitting.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against India Code — Constitution of India.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: Under Article 252, when may Parliament legislate on a matter in the State List for two or more States?
o: When those State Legislatures pass resolutions requesting Parliament to legislate
Whenever the Union Cabinet declares an emergency
Only after every State Governor issues an ordinance
Whenever the Rajya Sabha passes a simple majority resolution
questions.e: Article 252 provides a route based on State consent. If two or more State Legislatures resolve that Parliament should legislate on a State List matter, Parliament may enact a law for those States; other States may later adopt it by resolution.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against India Code — Constitution of India.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: A refundable security deposit is received by the Government and held in trust for the depositor. Under Article 266, where is such money ordinarily credited?
o: The Consolidated Fund of India as tax revenue
questions.e: Article 266 distinguishes the Consolidated Fund from the Public Account. Money received or held by Government in trust, such as deposits and similar liabilities, is credited to the Public Account rather than treated as ordinary tax revenue.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against India Code — Constitution of India.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: Under Article 267, the Contingency Fund of India is placed at whose disposal so that advances can be made for unforeseen expenditure pending legislative authorisation?
o: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
questions.e: Article 267 provides for a Contingency Fund placed at the disposal of the President. It enables advances for unforeseen expenditure until Parliament authorises the relevant expenditure through the constitutional budget process.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against India Code — Constitution of India.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: Under Article 315, who may provide by law for a Joint State Public Service Commission for two or more States?
o: The Governors acting jointly without legislation
The Union Public Service Commission by executive order
questions.e: Article 315(2) empowers Parliament to provide by law for a Joint State Public Service Commission for a group of two or more States. It is distinct from the ordinary arrangement of a separate State Public Service Commission.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against India Code — Constitution of India.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: Under Article 243-I, who constitutes the State Finance Commission to review the financial position of Panchayats?
o: The Speaker of the State Legislative Assembly
questions.e: Article 243-I requires the Governor to constitute a Finance Commission within the prescribed period and thereafter every five years. It reviews Panchayat finances and recommends principles for sharing taxes, grants and other financial resources.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against India Code — Constitution of India.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: A State Legislative Assembly wishes to create or abolish its Legislative Council. Under Article 169, what must the Assembly first pass?
o: A resolution by a majority of its total membership and at least two-thirds of members present and voting
A simple majority of members present and voting
A unanimous resolution of all elected members
A resolution approved by the Governor alone
questions.e: Article 169 requires a special resolution in the State Legislative Assembly: a majority of the total membership and not less than two-thirds of members present and voting. Parliament may then provide for creation or abolition by law.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against India Code — Constitution of India.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: Under Article 174, what is the maximum period that may intervene between the last sitting of one session of a State Legislature and the first sitting of its next session?
questions.e: Article 174 requires that six months shall not intervene between the last sitting in one session and the first sitting in the next. This ensures that the State Legislature is summoned at least twice in each year.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against India Code — Constitution of India.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: Article 243-G allows a State Legislature to endow Panchayats with powers and authority to function as institutions of self-government. Which area is expressly included?
o: Preparation of plans for economic development and social justice
questions.e: Article 243-G permits State Legislatures to devolve powers to Panchayats for economic development and social justice, including implementation of schemes relating to matters in the Eleventh Schedule. The extent of devolution is set by State law.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against India Code — Constitution of India.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: Under Article 243-H, which action may a State Legislature authorise a Panchayat to undertake by law?
o: Levy, collect and appropriate specified taxes, duties, tolls and fees
Impose customs duties on imports at international borders
Levy income tax on all residents of India
Issue currency notes for local development
questions.e: Article 243-H allows State law to authorise Panchayats to levy, collect and appropriate specified taxes, duties, tolls and fees. State law may also assign revenues, provide grants-in-aid and establish Panchayat funds.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against India Code — Constitution of India.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: In Mughal-period agrarian records, the term 'pahi-kashta' referred to which category of cultivators?
o: Non-resident cultivators who tilled land in a village other than their own
Peasants who owned no ploughs and worked only as soldiers
Revenue officers appointed by the village assembly
Cultivators who held hereditary rights over all village wasteland
questions.e: NCERT distinguishes khud-kashta, resident cultivators of the village, from pahi-kashta, cultivators who came from another village to cultivate land elsewhere. The distinction helps explain mobility and contractual cultivation in Mughal rural society.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against NCERT — Themes in Indian History II, Peasants, Zamindars and the State.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Themes in Indian History II, Peasants, Zamindars and the State

questions.q: In the Mughal mansabdari system, what did the two numerical ranks 'zat' and 'sawar' primarily indicate?
o: Zat indicated personal rank and salary; sawar indicated the cavalry obligation
Zat indicated land area; sawar indicated the tax rate on crops
Zat indicated religious status; sawar indicated court language
Zat indicated the number of villages; sawar indicated judicial authority
questions.e: NCERT explains that zat determined a mansabdar's rank and salary, while sawar specified the number of cavalrymen the mansabdar was required to maintain. The two figures therefore represented related but different aspects of service.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against NCERT — Our Pasts II, The Mughals.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Our Pasts II, The Mughals

questions.q: In the Mughal land classification described in the Ain-i Akbari, land left fallow for three to four years was called what?
questions.e: The four categories distinguished cultivation history: polaj was regularly cultivated, parauti was left fallow temporarily, chachar had remained fallow for three to four years, and banjar for five years or more. Chachar is therefore the correct category.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against NCERT — Themes in Indian History II, Peasants, Zamindars and the State.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Themes in Indian History II, Peasants, Zamindars and the State

questions.q: Under the Delhi Sultans, what was the principal responsibility of a muqti or iqtadar in the territory assigned to him?
o: To lead military campaigns and maintain law and order
To conduct the annual election of village headmen
To appoint the Sultan and determine succession
questions.e: NCERT describes muqtis as military commanders assigned iqtas. They led campaigns and maintained law and order, receiving revenue from their assignments as salary; state accountants checked collections and the required number of soldiers.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against NCERT — Our Pasts II, Delhi: 12th to 15th Century.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Our Pasts II, Delhi: 12th to 15th Century

questions.q: Which event in 1565 led to the sack of the Vijayanagara capital after the Battle of Talikota?
o: The defeat of Vijayanagara forces by a confederacy of Deccan Sultanates
The conquest of Hampi by the Portuguese
A Mughal invasion led by Akbar
A succession dispute between the Chola princes
questions.e: The Battle of Talikota in 1565 resulted in the defeat of Vijayanagara by a coalition of Deccan Sultanates. The capital was subsequently sacked, although the empire continued for some time from other centres.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against NCERT — Themes in Indian History I, An Imperial Capital: Vijayanagara.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Themes in Indian History I, An Imperial Capital: Vijayanagara

questions.q: Unlike the principle of primogeniture, what succession practice did the Mughals follow for inheritance among the emperor's sons?
o: Coparcenary division of inheritance among the sons
Automatic inheritance by the eldest son alone
questions.e: NCERT notes that the Mughals did not follow primogeniture. Their Timurid custom of coparcenary inheritance involved division of inheritance among the sons, a practice that could contribute to contests for power.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against NCERT — Our Pasts II, The Mughals.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Our Pasts II, The Mughals

questions.q: The point inside the Earth where an earthquake rupture begins is called the focus or hypocentre. What is the point directly above it on the Earth's surface called?
questions.e: The focus, also called the hypocentre, is the subsurface origin of the rupture. The epicentre is the point on the surface vertically above that focus; the two terms describe different locations and should not be interchanged.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against USGS — Earthquake Hazards Program.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: At a transform plate boundary, how do the two adjoining tectonic plates generally move relative to each other?
o: They slide horizontally past one another
They move directly towards each other and one must subduct
They move apart and new crust forms between them
One plate rises vertically above the other without lateral motion
questions.e: Transform boundaries involve lateral movement along a fault as plates slide past one another. They commonly produce earthquakes, but they do not primarily create or destroy crust in the way divergent and convergent boundaries do.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against USGS — Plate tectonics and plate boundaries.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: USGS — Plate tectonics and plate boundaries

questions.q: A ridge has a steep scarp slope on one side and a long, gentle dip slope on the other, reflecting erosion of gently inclined rock layers. What landform is this?
questions.e: A cuesta is an asymmetrical ridge developed on gently dipping strata. Differential erosion creates a steep scarp slope where resistant layers are exposed and a gentler dip slope that follows the inclination of the underlying beds.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against NCERT — Geography textbooks and curriculum.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: A river network has long parallel main streams joined by short tributaries that enter at nearly right angles in a folded mountain belt. Which drainage pattern is most likely?
questions.e: Trellis drainage commonly develops in folded or structurally controlled terrain where alternating resistant and less-resistant rock bands guide parallel valleys. Short tributaries join the main streams at near-right angles, creating a trellis-like plan.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against NCERT — Geography textbooks and curriculum.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: A long, narrow, deep sea inlet with steep sides occupies a valley that was first deepened by a glacier and later flooded by the sea. What is this landform called?
questions.e: A fjord is a drowned glacial valley. Glacial erosion deepens and steepens the valley, often below present sea level; after the ice retreats, seawater floods the valley to form a long, narrow inlet.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against NCERT — Geography textbooks and curriculum.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: A rock breaks down in place because of temperature changes and chemical reactions, but the fragments are not transported away. Which process is occurring?
questions.e: Weathering is the physical, chemical or biological breakdown of rock at or near the Earth's surface. Erosion includes the removal and transport of the loosened material by water, wind, ice or gravity.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against NCERT — Geography textbooks and curriculum.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: Which statement best describes the formation of a metamorphic rock?
o: An existing rock is altered by heat, pressure or chemically active fluids without completely melting
Magma cools and crystallises at or below the surface
Loose sediments are compacted and cemented into layers
Organic remains accumulate and harden into coal
questions.e: Metamorphism changes the mineral composition, texture or structure of an existing rock under heat, pressure or chemically active fluids. The rock remains solid during metamorphism; complete melting followed by cooling would produce igneous rock.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against NCERT — Geography textbooks and curriculum.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: Lateritic soils commonly develop in warm, wet regions where intense rainfall causes prolonged leaching. Which material tends to become relatively enriched in the soil profile?
o: Fresh soluble salts and unaltered carbonates
Pure quartz with no clay minerals
questions.e: Strong chemical weathering and leaching remove many soluble bases and silica from the upper soil profile. Iron and aluminium compounds are comparatively less mobile under these conditions and can become relatively concentrated in lateritic soils.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against NCERT — Geography textbooks and curriculum.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: What primarily drives the large-scale thermohaline circulation of the oceans?
o: Differences in seawater density caused by temperature and salinity
Only the daily rise and fall of tides
Only the direction of prevailing surface winds
Differences in ocean colour and transparency
questions.e: Thermohaline circulation is linked to density differences in seawater. Temperature and salinity both affect density; colder and/or saltier water is generally denser and can sink, helping drive deep-ocean circulation.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against NOAA — Ocean circulation and currents.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: A river mouth is funnel-shaped, strongly influenced by tides, and has little permanent accumulation of river sediment because tidal currents carry much of it away. Which landform is described?
questions.e: An estuary is a tidal river mouth where seawater and freshwater mix and tidal currents help keep channels open. A delta forms where sediment accumulates faster than waves and currents can remove it, often producing distributaries.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against NCERT — Geography textbooks and curriculum.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: Which pair consists of non-debt capital receipts of the Union Government?
o: Recovery of loans and disinvestment proceeds
questions.e: Non-debt capital receipts do not create a new repayment liability. The Union Budget and Economic Survey identify recovery of loans and disinvestment proceeds as major examples; taxes are revenue receipts and market borrowings are debt receipts.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against Union Budget — Budget at a Glance / receipts classification.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Union Budget — Budget at a Glance / receipts classification

questions.q: A country imports goods worth more than it exports, even though it has a surplus in services. What is the position of its merchandise trade balance?
o: It cannot be determined unless remittances are known
questions.e: The merchandise trade balance compares exports and imports of physical goods. If goods imports exceed goods exports, the merchandise balance is in deficit; a services surplus may improve the broader current account but does not change the goods-only result.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against RBI — Balance of Payments and external-sector publications.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: RBI — Balance of Payments and external-sector publications

questions.q: A sharp rise in household and government spending pushes aggregate demand beyond the economy's short-run productive capacity. What type of inflationary pressure is this?
questions.e: Demand-pull inflation arises when aggregate demand grows faster than the economy can supply goods and services at prevailing prices. Stronger spending bids for limited output and places upward pressure on the general price level.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against NCERT — Introductory Macroeconomics textbook portal.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: A sudden rise in fuel and transport costs increases firms' production expenses, causing them to raise selling prices. Which explanation best fits this situation?
o: A fall in the general price level
questions.e: Cost-push inflation begins with higher input costs, such as fuel, wages or imported raw materials. Firms may pass some costs to consumers, shifting short-run aggregate supply left and raising prices even without an initial demand boom.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against NCERT — Introductory Macroeconomics textbook portal.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: Under RBI prudential directions for commercial banks, a term-loan account is generally classified as an NPA when principal or interest remains overdue for more than what period?
questions.e: The RBI's asset-classification directions specify that a term loan becomes an NPA when interest and/or instalments of principal remain overdue for more than 90 days. The rule differs for some agricultural advances and other account types, so this item is limited to term loans.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against RBI — Prudential norms on Income Recognition, Asset Classification and Provisioning.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: RBI — Prudential norms on Income Recognition, Asset Classification and Provisioning

questions.q: How is the effective revenue deficit of the Union Government calculated?
o: Revenue deficit minus grants for creation of capital assets
Fiscal deficit plus non-debt capital receipts
questions.e: The Budget defines effective revenue deficit as revenue deficit less grants for creation of capital assets. The adjustment recognises that some expenditure booked as revenue grants is used by recipient bodies to create capital assets.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against Union Budget — Effective Revenue Deficit definition.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Union Budget — Effective Revenue Deficit definition

questions.q: When increased government borrowing absorbs available loanable funds and places upward pressure on interest rates, potentially reducing private investment, what is this effect called?
questions.e: The crowding-out effect describes how government borrowing may compete with private borrowers for available funds. If interest rates rise, some private investment projects may become too costly and be postponed or cancelled.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against NCERT — Introductory Macroeconomics textbook portal.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: The annual inflation rate falls from 6% to 3%, but the general price level is still rising. What is this situation called?
questions.e: Disinflation is a decline in the rate of inflation while the overall price level continues to rise. Deflation means a sustained fall in the general price level, so a positive inflation rate of 3% is disinflation, not deflation.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against NCERT — Introductory Macroeconomics textbook portal.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: Under a floating exchange-rate regime, a currency loses value because of market demand and supply. Which term is normally used for this change?
questions.e: Depreciation normally refers to a market-driven fall in a currency's value under a floating or flexible exchange-rate regime. Devaluation is an official downward adjustment of a currency's value by the authorities under a fixed or managed parity.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against RBI — Exchange-rate policy and exchange-rate terminology.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: RBI — Exchange-rate policy and exchange-rate terminology

questions.q: A country's export-price index rises relative to its import-price index. What does an improvement in its terms of trade generally mean?
o: A given quantity of exports can purchase more imports
A given quantity of exports can purchase fewer imports
The country must export fewer goods by law
The exchange rate must remain fixed
questions.e: Terms of trade compare export prices with import prices. When export prices rise relative to import prices, the country can generally obtain more imports for a given quantity of exports, although the overall trade balance also depends on quantities and demand.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against RBI — Balance of Payments and external-sector publications.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: RBI — Balance of Payments and external-sector publications

questions.q: A magnet is pushed towards a closed conducting coil. What does Lenz's law tell us about the direction of the induced current?
o: It produces a magnetic effect that opposes the change in flux causing it
It always produces a magnetic field in the direction of the magnet's motion
It always flows clockwise when viewed from the magnet side
It is independent of whether the magnet approaches or recedes
questions.e: Lenz's law states that the induced current flows in a direction whose magnetic effect opposes the change in magnetic flux that produced it. This is consistent with conservation of energy; the coil resists the approach of the magnet.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against NCERT — Science and Physics/Chemistry textbooks.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: Two resistors of 6 ohms and 3 ohms are connected in parallel. What is their equivalent resistance?
questions.e: For parallel resistors, 1/R = 1/6 + 1/3 = 1/6 + 2/6 = 3/6 = 1/2. Thus the equivalent resistance is 2 ohms, which is lower than the smallest individual resistance.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against NCERT — Science and Physics/Chemistry textbooks.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: During electrolysis, which process takes place at the cathode?
questions.e: Reduction occurs at the cathode because positively charged ions or other reducible species gain electrons there. Oxidation occurs at the anode; the electrode names do not change this rule in electrolytic cells.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against NCERT — Science and Physics/Chemistry textbooks.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: Why is DNA replication described as semi-conservative?
o: Each daughter DNA molecule contains one parental strand and one newly synthesised strand
Both strands of each daughter molecule are newly synthesised
One daughter molecule receives all the original DNA and the other receives none
The DNA sequence is copied without using a template
questions.e: In semi-conservative replication, the two parental strands separate and each acts as a template for a new complementary strand. Each resulting DNA double helix therefore conserves one original strand and contains one newly made strand.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against NCERT — Biology, Molecular Basis of Inheritance.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Biology, Molecular Basis of Inheritance

questions.q: Which statement best describes the normal role of insulin released by pancreatic beta cells?
o: It lowers blood glucose by promoting cellular uptake and storage of nutrients
It raises blood glucose by stimulating glycogen breakdown
It directly converts oxygen into glucose
It prevents all glucose from entering liver cells
questions.e: Insulin is secreted by beta cells of the pancreatic islets when blood glucose rises. It promotes glucose uptake in responsive tissues and supports storage as glycogen and fat, thereby lowering circulating blood glucose.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against NCERT — Science and Physics/Chemistry textbooks.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: During the light reactions of photosynthesis, which photosystem is associated with the splitting of water and release of oxygen?
questions.e: The oxygen-evolving complex associated with Photosystem II catalyses photolysis of water. This supplies electrons to the photosynthetic electron-transport chain and releases protons and molecular oxygen.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against NCERT — Science and Physics/Chemistry textbooks.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: Why are transformer cores commonly built from thin, insulated laminations rather than one solid block of iron?
o: To increase the resistance of the external load
To eliminate magnetic flux from the core
To convert alternating current into direct current
questions.e: Thin insulated laminations interrupt large circulating current paths inside the core. This increases the resistance of eddy-current loops and reduces heat loss, improving transformer efficiency.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against NCERT — Science and Physics/Chemistry textbooks.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: In a plant root, where is the Casparian strip located and what is its main role?
o: In the endodermis, where it blocks apoplastic flow and helps regulate entry into the vascular cylinder
In the epidermis, where it absorbs sunlight for photosynthesis
In the xylem vessels, where it transports sugars
In the phloem, where it prevents transpiration
questions.e: The Casparian strip is a band of suberin in endodermal cell walls. It interrupts the apoplastic route, forcing water and dissolved minerals to cross a selectively controlled membrane before entering the stele.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against NCERT — Biology Exemplar Problems, Class XI (plant water movement and Casparian strip).
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Biology Exemplar Problems, Class XI (plant water movement and Casparian strip)

questions.q: What is the main effect of a myelin sheath around many vertebrate nerve fibres?
o: It speeds impulse conduction by enabling saltatory conduction between nodes of Ranvier
It converts electrical impulses into hormones
It prevents all ion movement across the axon membrane
It stores neurotransmitters inside the nucleus
questions.e: Myelin electrically insulates much of the axon. Action potentials are regenerated at the nodes of Ranvier, so the impulse appears to jump from node to node; this saltatory conduction is faster than continuous propagation.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against NCERT — Science and Physics/Chemistry textbooks.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: A sound source moves towards a stationary listener. What happens to the frequency heard by the listener, compared with the emitted frequency?
o: It remains exactly the same in all cases
questions.e: When a source approaches a stationary listener, successive wavefronts arrive closer together. The observed wavelength is shorter and the observed frequency is higher; when the source recedes, the observed frequency is lower.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against NCERT — Physics syllabus and textbook resources.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Physics syllabus and textbook resources

questions.q: A wetland temporarily stores excess rainwater and releases it more slowly, reducing downstream flood peaks. Which ecosystem service is being illustrated?
questions.e: Wetlands can act as natural storage areas: water spreads across floodplains or shallow basins and is released gradually. This can reduce peak flows, while wetlands also provide habitat and water-purification benefits.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against MoEFCC — Convention on Wetlands / Ramsar framework.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: MoEFCC — Convention on Wetlands / Ramsar framework

questions.q: A stream-monitoring programme records the presence and condition of pollution-sensitive aquatic insects. What is the main purpose of using these organisms?
o: To infer environmental quality from biological responses
To measure the stream's exact depth without instruments
To calculate the age of the river channel
To identify the chemical formula of every dissolved mineral
questions.e: Bioindicators are organisms whose presence, absence, abundance or condition reflects environmental conditions. Pollution-sensitive aquatic insects can reveal ecological stress over time and complement one-time chemical measurements of water.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against MoEFCC — Convention on Biological Diversity.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: What does the ecological footprint of a population estimate?
o: The biologically productive area needed to supply its resource use and absorb its waste
The total number of animal species living in its territory
The physical area covered by buildings alone
The amount of rainfall received in one year
questions.e: The ecological footprint expresses human demand on biologically productive land and water. It estimates the area needed to provide consumed resources and assimilate certain wastes, especially carbon emissions, under prevailing technology and management.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against Global Footprint Network — Ecological Footprint.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: Why is a watershed often used as a planning unit for soil and water conservation?
o: Runoff, streams, land use and upstream activities are connected within the same drainage area
A watershed always follows administrative district boundaries
It contains only groundwater and excludes surface streams
Every watershed has the same rainfall and soil conditions
questions.e: A watershed is an area draining to a common outlet. Planning at this scale recognises that land cover, erosion, infiltration and upstream activities affect downstream water quantity and quality, so measures are coordinated across the drainage system.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against NCERT — Geography textbooks and curriculum (watershed and drainage-basin concepts).
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Geography textbooks and curriculum (watershed and drainage-basin concepts)

questions.q: What is an ecotone in ecology?
o: A transition zone between two adjacent ecosystems or ecological communities
A region where no living organisms can survive
A deep layer of permanently frozen soil
A single species occupying the entire food web
questions.e: An ecotone is a transition area between adjoining ecological communities, such as forest and grassland. It may contain species from both communities and sometimes species particularly adapted to the boundary conditions.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against MoEFCC — Convention on Biological Diversity.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: A vegetated strip is maintained alongside a stream to intercept sediment and pollutants in surface runoff before they enter the water. What is this strip commonly called?
questions.e: Vegetated buffers beside streams slow overland flow and help trap sediment and some pollutants through filtration, deposition, infiltration and plant uptake. They can also stabilise banks and provide habitat along waterways.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against USDA Natural Resources Conservation Service — Filter strips and runoff control.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: USDA Natural Resources Conservation Service — Filter strips and runoff control

questions.q: A narrow strip of suitable habitat connects two otherwise separated forest patches, allowing animals to move between them. What conservation function does it provide?
questions.e: An ecological corridor links habitat patches and can facilitate dispersal, migration and gene flow between populations. Connectivity can reduce isolation and support recolonisation, although corridor design must suit the species concerned.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against MoEFCC — Convention on Biological Diversity.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: After a disturbance, an ecosystem absorbs the shock, reorganises and continues to maintain its essential structure and functions. Which concept does this describe?
questions.e: Resilience describes the capacity of a system to absorb disturbance and reorganise while retaining its essential identity, functions and feedbacks. It is different from simply returning immediately to an identical pre-disturbance state.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against IPCC — Climate Change 2022: Impacts, Adaptation and Vulnerability.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: IPCC — Climate Change 2022: Impacts, Adaptation and Vulnerability

questions.q: A system performs a full backup on Sunday. On Monday it saves changes since Sunday; on Tuesday it saves changes since Monday's backup. What type of Tuesday backup is this?
questions.e: An incremental backup captures changes since the immediately preceding backup, whether that was full or incremental. A differential backup instead captures all changes since the last full backup, so the Tuesday set here is incremental.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against NIST — Contingency Planning Guide for Federal Information Systems.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NIST — Contingency Planning Guide for Federal Information Systems

questions.q: In a SQL query that groups sales by branch, which clause is used to filter individual rows before the grouping operation?
questions.e: WHERE filters rows before GROUP BY forms groups. HAVING filters the resulting groups, often using aggregate conditions such as SUM or COUNT; confusing the two can change the meaning of a query.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against PostgreSQL — SELECT, WHERE and HAVING clauses.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: PostgreSQL — SELECT, WHERE and HAVING clauses

questions.q: A staff login requires a password and a one-time code generated by a hardware token. Why is this multi-factor authentication?
o: It combines something the user knows with something the user has
It uses two different passwords, both things the user knows
It uses two usernames for the same account
It asks the user to repeat the same PIN twice
questions.e: NIST distinguishes factors such as something you know, something you have and something you are. A password is a knowledge factor and a controlled hardware token is a possession factor, so the login uses two distinct factor categories.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against NIST — Multi-factor authentication glossary.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: An attacker sends a customised fraudulent email to one named employee, referring to that employee's actual project and supervisor to induce a payment. What type of phishing is this?
questions.e: Spear phishing is a targeted form of phishing tailored to a particular person or organisation. Personalised details make the message appear credible, but the aim remains to trick the recipient into disclosing information or taking an unsafe action.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against NIST — Digital identity guidelines and phishing.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NIST — Digital identity guidelines and phishing

questions.q: Which network protocol automatically provides a client with configuration information such as an IP address, subnet mask and default gateway?
questions.e: DHCP automates the assignment of network configuration parameters to clients. It reduces manual configuration and allows a device to obtain an address lease and other settings when it joins a network.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against IETF — RFC 2131, Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: IETF — RFC 2131, Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol

questions.q: On an IPv4 local-area network, what does ARP help a host discover when it already knows the destination's IPv4 address on the local link?
o: The corresponding link-layer hardware address, usually a MAC address
questions.e: ARP resolves a protocol address such as an IPv4 address to a hardware address used for local-link delivery, commonly an Ethernet MAC address. It does not translate domain names or authenticate remote websites.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against IETF — RFC 826, Address Resolution Protocol.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: What do properly implemented digital signatures primarily provide for signed electronic data?
o: Authenticity and integrity, with support for non-repudiation
Confidentiality by hiding the entire message from every reader
Guaranteed protection from malware on the sender's device
Automatic deletion of the original document
questions.e: NIST describes a digital signature as a private-key operation verified with the corresponding public key. It supports origin authenticity and data integrity, and can support non-repudiation; it does not itself provide confidentiality.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against NIST — Digital signature glossary.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: Which statement correctly distinguishes a browser cache from an HTTP cookie?
o: A cache stores reusable responses or resources; a cookie stores small pieces of state sent with matching requests
A cache stores passwords only; a cookie stores complete web pages
A cache is always a server-side database; a cookie is a graphics file
Both are identical mechanisms for encrypting network traffic
questions.e: The browser cache can reuse stored responses such as images, scripts and other resources to reduce repeat downloads. Cookies store small state values, often for sessions or preferences, and may be sent with subsequent matching HTTP requests.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against MDN — HTTP caching and browser cookies.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: MDN — HTTP caching and browser cookies

questions.q: A bag contains 5 red and 3 blue balls. Two balls are drawn successively without replacement. What is the probability that both are red?
questions.e: The probability of a red ball first is 5/8. After one red is removed, 4 red remain among 7 balls, so the second-red probability is 4/7. Multiplying gives (5/8) × (4/7) = 20/56 = 5/14.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against NCERT — Mathematics Exemplar Problems.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: A map has a scale of 1:50,000. Two points are 3.6 cm apart on the map. What is their ground distance?
questions.e: At a scale of 1:50,000, 1 cm represents 50,000 cm or 500 m on the ground. Therefore 3.6 cm represents 3.6 × 500 = 1,800 m, which is 1.8 km.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against NCERT — Mathematics Exemplar Problems.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: The side of a square is increased by 25%. By what percentage does its area increase?
questions.e: Area varies as the square of the side. If the side becomes 1.25 times its original value, the area becomes 1.25² = 1.5625 times the original, so the increase is 0.5625 × 100 = 56.25%.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against NCERT — Mathematics Exemplar Problems.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: A rectangular plot measures 48 m by 30 m. A path 2 m wide runs inside along all four sides. What is the area of the path?
questions.e: The outer area is 48 × 30 = 1,440 m². Removing a 2 m strip on each side leaves an inner rectangle of 44 m by 26 m, or 1,144 m². The path area is 1,440 − 1,144 = 296 m².
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against NCERT — Mathematics Exemplar Problems.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: If x:y = 3:4, what is the value of the ratio (2x + 3y):(x + 2y)?
questions.e: Let x = 3k and y = 4k. Then 2x + 3y = 6k + 12k = 18k, while x + 2y = 3k + 8k = 11k. Cancelling k gives 18:11, because a common multiplier does not change a ratio.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against NCERT — Mathematics Exemplar Problems.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: A rainfall depth of 25 mm falls uniformly over a catchment area of 2 hectares. What volume of water falls on the area, ignoring infiltration and runoff?
questions.e: Convert 25 mm to 0.025 m and 2 hectares to 20,000 m². Volume = depth × area = 0.025 × 20,000 = 500 cubic metres. The calculation estimates gross rainfall volume before losses.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against NCERT — Mathematics Exemplar Problems.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: Mira is the sister of Nikhil. Nikhil is the father of Tara. How is Mira related to Tara?
questions.e: Nikhil is Tara's father, and Mira is Nikhil's sister. A father's sister is the child's paternal aunt. The relationship is determined through the parent-child link first, then the sibling link.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against Original Practice — author-created reasoning item.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: If 1 January 2024 was a Monday, what day of the week was 1 January 2025? (2024 was a leap year.)
questions.e: A leap year has 366 days, which is 52 weeks plus 2 days. The same calendar date therefore moves forward by two weekdays: Monday plus two days is Wednesday.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against Original Practice — author-created reasoning item.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: Five officers A, B, C, D and E sit equally spaced around a circular table facing the centre. B is immediately clockwise from A, C is second clockwise from A, and D is immediately anticlockwise from A. Who is immediately clockwise from C?
questions.e: Fix A at one seat and move clockwise: B occupies the next seat and C the second seat. D is immediately anticlockwise from A, leaving E in the only remaining seat, immediately clockwise from C.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against Original Practice — author-created reasoning item.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: A code replaces each English letter with the letter in the opposite position of the alphabet (A↔Z, B↔Y, and so on). How is the word TAX coded?
questions.e: The opposite-position mapping pairs the first and last letters, so T maps to G, A maps to Z and X maps to C. Reading the mapped letters in the original order gives GZC.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against Original Practice — author-created reasoning item.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: An analogue clock shows 2:35. What time would its mirror image show in a plane mirror?
questions.e: For a standard clock-face mirror image, subtract the shown time from 11:60. Thus 11:60 − 2:35 = 9:25. The result is the reflected clock reading, not the actual passage of time.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against Original Practice — author-created reasoning item.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: Choose the grammatically correct completion: 'The officer to ___ the records were forwarded acknowledged receipt.'
questions.e: In formal written English, whom is used as the object of a preposition referring to a person. Here the preposition 'to' directly governs the relative pronoun, so 'to whom' is the correct construction.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against Cambridge Dictionary — Relative pronouns.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: Which sentence is correctly punctuated as a non-defining relative clause?
o: The Shillong office, which opened in April, serves several districts.
The Shillong office, that opened in April, serves several districts.
The Shillong office, who opened in April, serves several districts.
The Shillong office, whose opened in April, serves several districts.
questions.e: A non-defining relative clause adds extra information and is set off by commas. In standard written English it uses a relative pronoun such as which or who, not that, and the clause is closed by a second comma.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against Cambridge Dictionary — Relative pronouns.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: Choose the correct completion: 'If the records were complete, the audit ___ much faster.'
questions.e: The sentence describes an unreal or hypothetical present situation. The second conditional commonly uses 'if + past simple' followed by 'would + base verb', so 'would proceed' is the correct form.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against Cambridge Dictionary — Relative pronouns.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: In the sentence 'The district officer, a trained surveyor, checked the map,' what is the grammatical function of 'a trained surveyor'?
o: An appositive phrase that renames the district officer
A direct object receiving the action
questions.e: An appositive is a noun or noun phrase placed beside another noun to identify or explain it. Here 'a trained surveyor' renames 'the district officer' and is set off by commas as additional information.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against Cambridge Dictionary — Relative pronouns.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: Choose the correct pair: 'The revised procedure may ___ processing time; its overall ___ will be reviewed after one month.'
questions.e: Affect is commonly used as a verb meaning to influence, while effect is commonly a noun meaning result. The first blank needs a verb and the second a noun, so 'affect; effect' is correct.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against Cambridge Dictionary — Affect and effect.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: Choose the correct pair: 'The vehicle remained ___ while the clerk arranged the office ___.'
questions.e: Stationary means not moving, whereas stationery refers to writing materials such as paper, envelopes and pens. The sentence needs the adjective for the vehicle and the noun for office supplies.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against Cambridge Dictionary — Stationary and stationery.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: Choose the correct pair: 'The blue tie will ___ the suit, and the visitor paid the clerk a kind ___.'
questions.e: Complement means to complete or go well with something; compliment means an expression of praise. The tie goes well with the suit, while the visitor gives praise, so the two words have different spellings and meanings.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Verified against Cambridge Dictionary — Complement and compliment.
questions.label: Original Practice
